html:
The Arabs are a people of the Arabian peninsula and, since the 600s CE, of most of West Asia and North Africa, united by the Arabic language. On the map the name marks the peoples of the Arabian interior in 200 BCE, and again in 1492 and 1500, outside the states of the coasts.

The first written mention of Arabs is in Assyrian records: in 853 BCE an Arab chief named Gindibu sent camels to fight the Assyrian king. For the next thousand years Arab tribes lived as camel herders, oasis farmers and caravan traders, and founded kingdoms on the desert's edges, such as the Nabataeans of Petra.

In the 600s the Prophet Muhammad united the tribes under Islam. In the Arab conquests that followed, armies from Arabia took the lands from Spain to Central Asia, and the caliphs ruled them in Arabic. Over the following centuries many conquered peoples, from Iraq to Morocco, came to speak Arabic and to count themselves Arabs.

Inside Arabia, tribes and small emirates kept much of their old way of life, under loose Ottoman claims, until the rise of the Saudi state in modern times.
